@tailwind components;
@tailwind utilities;

@layer base {
  /* ... (Default theme styles) ... */
  :root {
    --background: 0 0% 100%;
    --foreground: 222.2 84% 4.9%;

    --muted: 210 40% 96.1%;
    --muted-foreground: 215.4 16.3% 46.9%;

    --card-foreground: 222.2 84% 4.9%;

    --error: 0 84.2% 60.2%;
    --error-foreground: 210 40% 98%;

    --success: 159 52% 39%;
    --success-foreground: 0 85.7% 97.3%;

    --warning: 36 93% 56%;
    --warning-foreground: 0 85.7% 97.3%;

    --ring: 215 20.2% 65.1%;

    --radius: 0.5rem;
  }

  /* ... (Dark theme styles) ... */
  .dark {
    --background: 222.2 84% 4.9%;

Alert from '@zyxui/alert';
import { AlertCircleIcon, AlertTriangleIcon, CheckCircleIcon } from 'lucide-react';

<Alert
    title='Default Color (No Icon)'
    color='default'
    description={
        <span className='text-inherit'>
            This is a default color alert description! This example also shows that you can use alert without icon props.
        </span>
    }
/>
<hr className='my-4' />
<Alert
    title='Error Color (With Icon)'
    color='error'
    icon={<AlertCircleIcon />}
    description={
        <span className='text-inherit'>
            This is an error color alert description!
        </span>
    }
/>
<hr className='my-4' />
<Alert
    title='Warning Color'
    color='warning'
    icon={<AlertTriangleIcon />}
    description={
        <span className='text-inherit'>
            This is a warning color alert description!
        </span>
    }
/>
<hr className='my-4' />
<Alert
    title='Success Color'
    color='success'
    icon={<CheckCircleIcon />}
    description={
        <span className='text-inherit'>
            This is a success color alert description!
        </span>
    }
/>

    color='success'
    icon={<CheckCircleIcon />}
    description={
        <span className='text-inherit'>
            This is a success color alert description!
        </span>
    }
/>

import { Preview, Example, Command } from '@/components/mdx/components';
import Avatar from '@zyxui/avatar';
import { User, Star, Camera } from 'lucide-react';

# Avatar

The `Avatar` component is a versatile element for displaying user profile pictures, initials, or icons. Perfect for user interfaces, comment sections, and user lists.

## Installation

Ensure that you have the @zyxui library installed in your project:
<Example>
```bash
pnpm add @zyxui/avatar
```
</Example>

If you haven't installed and setup @zyxui before, please follow the [`installation guide`](/docs/installation)

## Basic Avatar

The most basic usage of the Avatar component with different content types.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-4 items-center'>
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a042581f4e29026704d" alt="User 1" />
    <Avatar fallback="JD" color="primary" />
    <Avatar icon={<User />} color="secondary" />
    <Avatar src="/invalid.jpg" fallback={<Camera />} color="danger" />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Avatar } from '@zyxui/avatar';
  import { User, Camera } from 'lucide-react';

  export const BasicAvatarExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a042581f4e29026704d" alt="User 1" />
        <Avatar fallback="JD" color="primary" />
        <Avatar icon={<User />} color="secondary" />
        <Avatar src="/invalid.jpg" fallback={<Camera />} color="danger" />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

## Customization

The `Avatar` component is <ins>**highly customizable**</ins>, offering various options to match your design needs:

### Sizes

Available in different sizes to fit various layouts.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-4 items-center'>
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a042581f4e29026704d" size="sm" alt="Small" />
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a04258114e29026702d" size="md" alt="Medium" />
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a042581f4e29026024d" size="lg" alt="Large" />
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a04258a24e29026704e" size="xl" alt="Extra Large" />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Avatar } from '@zyxui/avatar';

  export const AvatarSizesExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Avatar src="..." size="sm" alt="Small" />
        <Avatar src="..." size="md" alt="Medium" />
        <Avatar src="..." size="lg" alt="Large" />
        <Avatar src="..." size="xl" alt="Extra Large" />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

### Shapes

Choose between circular or square shapes.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-4 items-center'>
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a042581f4e29026704d" shape="circle" alt="Circle" />
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a04258114e29026702d" shape="square" alt="Square" />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Avatar } from '@zyxui/avatar';

  export const AvatarShapesExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Avatar src="..." shape="circle" alt="Circle" />
        <Avatar src="..." shape="square" alt="Square" />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

### Colors and Fallbacks

Customize the background color when displaying fallback content.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-3 items-center'>
    <Avatar fallback="DF" color="default" />
    <Avatar fallback="PR" color="primary" />
    <Avatar fallback="SC" color="secondary" />
    <Avatar fallback="SU" color="success" />
    <Avatar fallback="WA" color="warning" />
    <Avatar fallback="DA" color="danger" />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Avatar } from '@zyxui/avatar';

  export const AvatarColorsExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Avatar fallback="DF" color="default" />
        <Avatar fallback="PR" color="primary" />
        <Avatar fallback="SC" color="secondary" />
        <Avatar fallback="SU" color="success" />
        <Avatar fallback="WA" color="warning" />
        <Avatar fallback="DA" color="danger" />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

## Real-World Examples

### User Status

Display user status with customizable indicators.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-4 items-center'>
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a042581f4e29026704d" status="online" alt="Online" />
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a04258114e29026702d" status="offline" alt="Offline" />
    <Avatar src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a04258a24e29026704e" status="away" alt="Away" />
    <Avatar fallback="SB" color="success" status="busy" alt="Busy" />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Avatar } from '@zyxui/avatar';

  export const UserStatusExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Avatar src="..." status="online" alt="Online" />
        <Avatar src="..." status="offline" alt="Offline" />
        <Avatar src="..." status="away" alt="Away" />
        <Avatar fallback="SB" color="success" status="busy" alt="Busy" />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

### Interactive Avatars

Create interactive avatars with borders and hover effects.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-4 items-center'>
    <Avatar
      src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?u=a042581f4e29026704d"
      bordered
      className="cursor-pointer hover:opacity-80"
      alt="Interactive"
    />
    <Avatar
      fallback="JD"
      color="primary"
      bordered
      className="cursor-pointer hover:opacity-80"
    />
    <Avatar
      icon={<User />}
      color="secondary"
      bordered
      className="cursor-pointer hover:opacity-80"
    />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Avatar } from '@zyxui/avatar';
  import { User } from 'lucide-react';

  export const InteractiveAvatarExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Avatar
          src="..."
          bordered
          className="cursor-pointer hover:opacity-80"
          alt="Interactive"
        />
        <Avatar
          fallback="JD"
          color="primary"
          bordered
          className="cursor-pointer hover:opacity-80"
        />
        <Avatar
          icon={<User />}
          color="secondary"
          bordered
          className="cursor-pointer hover:opacity-80"
        />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

## API Reference

### Avatar

The Avatar component extends `HTMLDivElement` and includes the following props:

| Prop             | Type                                                            | Default        | Description                                                                 |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `src`            | `string`                                                        | -              | The URL of the image to display                                            |
| `alt`            | `string`                                                        | `''`          | Alt text for the image, also used for initial generation if no fallback    |
| `icon`           | `React.ReactNode`                                               | -              | A custom icon to display as a fallback if `src` is invalid                 |
| `fallback`       | `React.ReactNode`                                               | -              | Custom content to display if `src` is invalid. Takes precedence over `icon` |
| `size`           | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'`                                     | `'md'`         | The size of the avatar                                                     |
| `shape`          | `'circle' \| 'square'`                                          | `'circle'`     | The shape of the avatar                                                    |
| `color`          | `'default' \| 'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'default'`    | The background color when displaying fallback content        |
| `bordered`       | `boolean`                                                       | `false`        | If `true`, adds a border to the avatar                                   |
| `disabled`       | `boolean`                                                       | `false`        | If `true`, applies a disabled style                             |
| `status`         | `'online' \| 'offline' \| 'away' \| 'busy'`                           | -              | Shows a status indicator                                |
| `statusPosition` | `'top-right' \| 'bottom-right' \| 'top-left' \| 'bottom-left'`         | `'bottom-right'` | Position of the status indicator                                                 |

### Accessibility

- Always provide meaningful `alt` text for avatar images
- Use `aria-label` when the avatar represents a user or entity
- Ensure interactive avatars are keyboard accessible and have appropriate ARIA attributes
- Consider using `aria-live` regions for status changes

import { Preview, Example, Command } from '@/components/mdx/components';
import Badge from '@zyxui/badge';
import Button from '@zyxui/button';
import { Mail, ShoppingCart } from 'lucide-react';

# Badge

The `Badge` component is a versatile element used to highlight status, display counts, or mark content with short labels. Perfect for notifications, status indicators, and labeling items.

## Installation

Ensure that you have the @zyxui library installed in your project:
<Example>
```bash
pnpm add @zyxui/badge
```
</Example>

If you haven't installed and setup @zyxui before, please follow the [`installation guide`](/docs/installation)

## Basic Badge

The most basic usage of the Badge component is to display a simple label or count.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-4 items-center'>
    <Badge content="New" />
    <Badge content={5} color="primary" />
    <Badge content="Beta" variant="outline" />
    <Badge dot color="success" />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Badge } from '@zyxui/badge';

  export const BasicBadgeExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Badge content="New" />
        <Badge content={5} color="primary" />
        <Badge content="Beta" variant="outline" />
        <Badge dot color="success" />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

## Customization

The `Badge` component is <ins>**highly customizable**</ins>, offering various options to match your design needs:

### Colors

Choose from a range of predefined colors to convey different meanings.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-3 items-center'>
    <Badge content="Default" />
    <Badge content="Primary" color="primary" />
    <Badge content="Secondary" color="secondary" />
    <Badge content="Success" color="success" />
    <Badge content="Warning" color="warning" />
    <Badge content="Danger" color="danger" />
    <Badge content="Info" color="info" />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Badge } from '@zyxui/badge';

  export const BadgeColorsExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Badge content="Default" />
        <Badge content="Primary" color="primary" />
        <Badge content="Secondary" color="secondary" />
        <Badge content="Success" color="success" />
        <Badge content="Warning" color="warning" />
        <Badge content="Danger" color="danger" />
        <Badge content="Info" color="info" />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

### Variants

Different visual styles to suit various use cases.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-3 items-center'>
    <Badge content="Solid" variant="solid" color="primary" />
    <Badge content="Outline" variant="outline" color="primary" />
    <Badge content="Ghost" variant="ghost" color="primary" />
    <Badge dot variant="dot" color="primary" />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Badge } from '@zyxui/badge';

  export const BadgeVariantsExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Badge content="Solid" variant="solid" color="primary" />
        <Badge content="Outline" variant="outline" color="primary" />
        <Badge content="Ghost" variant="ghost" color="primary" />
        <Badge dot variant="dot" color="primary" />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

### Sizes

Available in different sizes to match your content scale.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-3 items-center'>
    <Badge content="Small" size="sm" color="secondary" />
    <Badge content="Medium" size="md" color="secondary" />
    <Badge content="Large" size="lg" color="secondary" />
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Badge } from '@zyxui/badge';

  export const BadgeSizesExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Badge content="Small" size="sm" color="secondary" />
        <Badge content="Medium" size="md" color="secondary" />
        <Badge content="Large" size="lg" color="secondary" />
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

## Real-World Examples

### Notification Badges

Common use case for displaying notification counts on icons or buttons.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-6 items-center'>
    <Badge content={3} color="danger">
      <Mail className="w-6 h-6" />
    </Badge>
    <Badge content="99+" color="primary">
      <Button size="sm">Messages</Button>
    </Badge>
    <Badge dot color="success">
      <ShoppingCart className="w-6 h-6" />
    </Badge>
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Badge } from '@zyxui/badge';
  import { Mail, ShoppingCart } from 'lucide-react';
  import { Button } from '@zyxui/button';

  export const NotificationBadgesExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Badge content={3} color="danger">
          <Mail className="w-6 h-6" />
        </Badge>
        <Badge content="99+" color="primary">
          <Button size="sm">Messages</Button>
        </Badge>
        <Badge dot color="success">
          <ShoppingCart className="w-6 h-6" />
        </Badge>
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

### Status Indicators

Use badges to show status or progress.

<Example>
  <Preview className='flex flex-wrap gap-4 items-center'>
    <Badge content="Active" color="success" variant="ghost" />
    <Badge content="Pending" color="warning" variant="outline" />
    <Badge content="Failed" color="danger" />
    <Badge dot color="success">Online</Badge>
  </Preview>

  ```jsx showLineNumbers
  import { Badge } from '@zyxui/badge';

  export const StatusBadgesExample = () => {
    return (
      <>
        <Badge content="Active" color="success" variant="ghost" />
        <Badge content="Pending" color="warning" variant="outline" />
        <Badge content="Failed" color="danger" />
        <Badge dot color="success">Online</Badge>
      </>
    )
  }
  ```
</Example>

## API Reference

### Badge

The Badge component extends `HTMLSpanElement` and includes the following props:

| Prop        | Type                                                                              | Default     | Description                                                                                                |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `content`   | `React.ReactNode`                                                                 | -           | The content to display inside the badge                                            |
| `max`       | `number`                                                                          | `99`        | Maximum value to display. If `content` is a number and exceeds `max`, it will show `{max}+`                |
| `showZero`  | `boolean`                                                                         | `false`     | If `true`, the badge will be visible when `content` is `0`                    |
| `dot`       | `boolean`                                                                         | `false`     | If `true`, renders the badge as a small dot, ignoring `content`      |
| `variant`   | `'solid' \| 'outline' \| 'ghost' \| 'dot'`                                           | `'solid'`   | The visual style of the badge                                                                             |
| `color`     | `'default' \| 'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info'` | `'default'` | The color scheme of the badge                                                                               |
| `size`      | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                                                                | `'md'`      | The size of the badge                                                    |
| `shape`     | `'rounded' \| 'pill'`                                                              | `'pill'`    | The shape of the badge                                                                                    |
| `invisible` | `boolean`                                                                         | `false`     | If `true`, the badge is not rendered                                                                      |

### Accessibility

- For decorative badges (like dots), use `aria-hidden="true"` to hide them from screen readers
- For informative badges (like counts), ensure the content is meaningful and accessible
- When wrapping interactive elements, make sure the badge content is properly announced with the interactive element

body.raw: import Button from '@zyxui/button'; import Alert from '@zyxui/alert'; import { AlertCircleIcon, SparkleIcon, GithubIcon } from 'lucide-react'; # Button The `Button` element in web development is an HTML element used to create interactive buttons that users can click or tap to trigger specific actions or functions on a web page. The ` ```jsx showLineNumbers import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const BasicButtonExample = () => { return ( ) } ``` ## Customization The `Button` component is **highly customizable**, allowing you to fine-tune its appearance and behavior to align with your project's unique requirements. Explore the following customization options: ### Colors Our `Button` component offers a color palette with options such as `default`, `error`, `warning`, and `success`. To customize these default colors to align with your project's aesthetics, [`consult How to customize themes in @@zyxui/button`](#). ```jsx showLineNumbers import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const ButtonWithColorsExample = () => { return ( ) } ``` ### Variants Modify `Button` styles effortlessly using the `variant` prop, with options like `solid`, `bordered`, `light`, `ghost`, `flat`, and `shadow`. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const ButtonWithVariants = () => { return ( ) } ``` ### Sizes Resize your `buttons` effortlessly with the size prop. Choose from `sm` (Small), `md` (Medium), or `lg` (Large) to control the button dimensions. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const ButtonWithSizes = () => { return ( ) } ``` ### Radiuses Easily customize the `border-radius` of your button using the `radius` prop, with options like `sm`,`md`, `lg`, `circle`, or `none`. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const ButtonWithRadiuses = () => { return ( ) } ``` ### Start Content The `startContent` prop allows you to seamlessly incorporate `ReactNode` elements at the beginning of a button's child. For instance, you can employ this feature to place an `icon` at the start of a button. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const ButtonWithStartContent = () => { return ( ) } ``` ### End Content The `endContent` prop enables the addition of `ReactNode` elements at the end of a button's child. For instance, this feature is ideal for appending an `icon` to the button's end. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const ButtonWithEndContent = () => { return ( ) } ``` ### Start & End Content Here are more examples to show you that [`startContent`](#start-content) & [`endContent`](#end-content) can be used together! ```jsx showLineNumbers import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const ButtonWithStartAndEndContent = () => { return ( ) } ``` ### Icon Only Create icon-only buttons with ease using the `iconOnly` prop. Use icons from libraries or custom SVGs to design your unique buttons. } description={It is highly recommended to leverage the extensive collection of icons available in the `lucide-react` icon library. This library offers a vast selection of beautifully crafted icons to enhance your design.} /> ```jsx showLineNumbers import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const IconOnlyButtons = () => { return ( ) } ``` ## API Reference For an in-depth exploration of available props and advanced usage, consult the `Button` component's API reference: | Property | Description | Type | Default | | --------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------|-------------| | className | Adding custom class names to your button. | `string` | `undefined` | | color | Customize button color styles. | `default` \| `error` \| `warning` \| `success` | `default` | | variant | Change button hover and base styles. | `solid` \| `bordered` \| `light` \| `ghost` \| `flat` \| `shadow` | `solid` | | size | Adjust button size to your specifications. | `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` | `md` | | radius | Change button border radius style. | `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `circle` \| `none` | `md` | | iconOnly | Craft buttons with exclusive focus on icons. | `boolean` | `false` | | startContent | Enrich buttons with content at the start [`see example`](#start-content). | `ReactNode` \| `undefined` | `undefined` | | endContent | Elevate buttons with content at the end. [`see example`](#end-content) | `ReactNode` \| `undefined` | `undefined` |

# Card The `Card` component is a flexible container that groups related content and actions. It provides a clean, organized way to display information with support for headers, body content, and footer actions. Perfect for creating product cards, user profiles, articles, and more. ## Installation Ensure that you have the @zyxui library installed in your project: ```bash npm install @zyxui/card ``` If you haven't installed and setup @zyxui before, please follow the [`installation guide`](/docs/installation) ## Basic Card To create a basic card, simply use the Card component with some content. It will inherit the default elevated styling.

This is a basic card with some content inside.

 ```jsx showLineNumbers import { Card, CardBody } from '@zyxui/card'; export const BasicCardExample = () => { return (

This is a basic card with some content inside.

 ) } ``` ## Card Structure The Card component consists of multiple sub-components that work together to create a structured layout. Card Title This is a description that provides more context about the card content.

This is the main content area of the card where you can place any content.

 ```jsx showLineNumbers import { Card, CardHeader, CardBody, CardFooter, CardTitle, CardDescription } from '@zyxui/card'; import Button from '@zyxui/button'; export const StructuredCardExample = () => { return ( Card Title This is a description that provides more context about the card content.

This is the main content area of the card where you can place any content.

 ) } ``` ## Customization The `Card` component is **highly customizable**, allowing you to fine-tune its appearance and behavior to align with your project's unique requirements. Explore the following customization options: ### Variants Modify `Card` styles effortlessly using the `variant` prop, with options like `elevated`, `outlined`, `filled`, and `ghost`. Elevated Card

This card has a shadow effect.

 Outlined Card

This card has a border outline.

 Filled Card

This card has a filled background.

 Ghost Card

This card has a transparent background.

 ```jsx showLineNumbers import { Card, CardHeader, CardBody, CardTitle } from '@zyxui/card'; export const CardVariantsExample = () => { return ( <> Elevated Card

This card has a shadow effect.

 Outlined Card

This card has a border outline.

 Filled Card

This card has a filled background.

 Ghost Card

This card has a transparent background.

 ) } ``` ### Sizes Resize your `cards` effortlessly with the size prop. Choose from `sm` (Small), `md` (Medium), or `lg` (Large) to control the card padding. Small Card

This card has small padding.

 Medium Card

This card has medium padding.

 Large Card

This card has large padding.

 ```jsx showLineNumbers import { Card, CardHeader, CardBody, CardTitle } from '@zyxui/card'; export const CardSizesExample = () => { return ( <> Small Card

This card has small padding.

 Medium Card

This card has medium padding.

 Large Card

This card has large padding.

 ) } ``` ### Hoverable Cards Make cards interactive with the `hoverable` prop, which adds hover effects and indicates clickability. Hoverable Card Hover over this card to see the interaction effect.

This card responds to hover with a scale effect.

 ```jsx showLineNumbers import { Card, CardHeader, CardBody, CardTitle, CardDescription } from '@zyxui/card'; export const HoverableCardExample = () => { return ( Hoverable Card Hover over this card to see the interaction effect.

This card responds to hover with a scale effect.

 ) } ``` ### Clickable Cards Cards can be made clickable by adding an `onClick` handler, which automatically makes them hoverable. alert('Card clicked!')} className="w-80"> Clickable Card Click this card to trigger an action.

This entire card is clickable and will show an alert when clicked.

 ```jsx showLineNumbers import { Card, CardHeader, CardBody, CardTitle, CardDescription } from '@zyxui/card'; export const ClickableCardExample = () => { return ( alert('Card clicked!')} className="w-80"> Clickable Card Click this card to trigger an action.

This entire card is clickable and will show an alert when clicked.

 ) } ``` ### Border Radius Easily customize the `border-radius` of your card using the `radius` prop, with options like `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, or `none`.

No radius

import Button from '@zyxui/button';

    <Card className="w-80">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Card Title</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>
          This is a description that provides more context about the card content.
        </CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>

        <p>This is the main content area of the card where you can place any content.</p>
      </CardBody>
      <CardFooter>
        <Button size="sm">Action</Button>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">Cancel</Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  )
}

export const CardVariantsExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <Card variant='elevated' className="w-64">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Elevated Card</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardBody>
          <p>This card has a shadow effect.</p>
        </CardBody>
      </Card>

      <Card variant='outlined' className="w-64">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Outlined Card</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardBody>
          <p>This card has a border outline.</p>
        </CardBody>
      </Card>

      <Card variant='filled' className="w-64">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Filled Card</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardBody>
          <p>This card has a filled background.</p>
        </CardBody>
      </Card>

      <Card variant='ghost' className="w-64">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Ghost Card</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardBody>
          <p>This card has a transparent background.</p>
        </CardBody>
      </Card>
    </>
  )
}

{ Card, CardHeader, CardBody, CardFooter, CardTitle, CardDescription } from '@zyxui/card';
import Button from '@zyxui/button';
import { BookmarkIcon, HeartIcon, ShareIcon, StarIcon } from 'lucide-react';

export const ProductCardExample = () => {
  return (
    <Card className="w-80" hoverable>
      <CardHeader>
        <div className="flex justify-between items-start">
          <div>
            <CardTitle>Premium Headphones</CardTitle>
            <CardDescription>Wireless noise-cancelling headphones</CardDescription>
          </div>
          <BookmarkIcon size={20} className="text-gray-400 hover:text-gray-600 cursor-pointer" />
        </div>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>
        <div className="space-y-2">
          <div className="flex items-center space-x-1">
            {[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((star) => (
              <StarIcon key={star} size={16} className="fill-yellow-400 text-yellow-400" />
            ))}
            <span className="text-sm text-gray-600 ml-2">4.8 (124 reviews)</span>
          </div>
          <p className="text-2xl font-bold">$299</p>
          <p className="text-sm text-gray-600">Free shipping \u2022 30-day returns</p>
        </div>
      </CardBody>
      <CardFooter className="space-x-2">
        <Button className="flex-1">Add to Cart</Button>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
          <HeartIcon size={16} />
        </Button>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
          <ShareIcon size={16} />
        </Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  )
}

import Button from '@zyxui/button';
import { BookmarkIcon, HeartIcon, ShareIcon, StarIcon } from 'lucide-react';

export const ProductCardExample = () => {
  return (
    <Card className="w-80" hoverable>
      <CardHeader>
        <div className="flex justify-between items-start">
          <div>
            <CardTitle>Premium Headphones</CardTitle>
            <CardDescription>Wireless noise-cancelling headphones</CardDescription>
          </div>
          <BookmarkIcon size={20} className="text-gray-400 hover:text-gray-600 cursor-pointer" />
        </div>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>
        <div className="space-y-2">
          <div className="flex items-center space-x-1">
            {[1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((star) => (
              <StarIcon key={star} size={16} className="fill-yellow-400 text-yellow-400" />
            ))}
            <span className="text-sm text-gray-600 ml-2">4.8 (124 reviews)</span>
          </div>
          <p className="text-2xl font-bold">$299</p>
          <p className="text-sm text-gray-600">Free shipping \u2022 30-day returns</p>
        </div>
      </CardBody>
      <CardFooter className="space-x-2">
        <Button className="flex-1">Add to Cart</Button>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
          <HeartIcon size={16} />
        </Button>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
          <ShareIcon size={16} />
        </Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  )
}

{ Card, CardHeader, CardBody, CardFooter, CardTitle, CardDescription } from '@zyxui/card';
import Button from '@zyxui/button';
import { MoreVerticalIcon, HeartIcon, ShareIcon } from 'lucide-react';

export const ArticleCardExample = () => {
  return (
    <Card className="w-96" hoverable>
      <CardHeader>
        <div className="flex justify-between items-start">
          <div className="space-y-1">
            <CardTitle>Building Better User Interfaces</CardTitle>
            <CardDescription>
              Learn the fundamentals of creating intuitive and accessible user interfaces.
            </CardDescription>
            <div className="flex items-center space-x-2 text-sm text-gray-500">
              <span>John Doe</span>
              <span>\u2022</span>
              <span>5 min read</span>
              <span>\u2022</span>
              <span>March 15, 2024</span>
            </div>
          </div>
          <MoreVerticalIcon size={20} className="text-gray-400 hover:text-gray-600 cursor-pointer" />
        </div>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>
        <p className="text-gray-600">
          Discover the principles and best practices for designing user interfaces that are both
          beautiful and functional. This guide covers everything from layout fundamentals to
          accessibility considerations.
        </p>
      </CardBody>
      <CardFooter>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">Read More</Button>
        <div className="flex space-x-2 ml-auto">
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
            <HeartIcon size={16} />
          </Button>
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
            <ShareIcon size={16} />
          </Button>
        </div>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  )
}

import { MoreVerticalIcon, HeartIcon, ShareIcon } from 'lucide-react';

  return (
    <Card className="w-96" hoverable>
      <CardHeader>
        <div className="flex justify-between items-start">
          <div className="space-y-1">
            <CardTitle>Building Better User Interfaces</CardTitle>
            <CardDescription>

            </CardDescription>

        </div>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>
        <p className="text-gray-600">
          Discover the principles and best practices for designing user interfaces that are both
          beautiful and functional. This guide covers everything from layout fundamentals to
          accessibility considerations.
        </p>
      </CardBody>
      <CardFooter>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">Read More</Button>
        <div className="flex space-x-2 ml-auto">
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
            <HeartIcon size={16} />
          </Button>
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
            <ShareIcon size={16} />
          </Button>
        </div>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  )
}

import Text from '@zyxui/text'
import Button from '@zyxui/button'
import { useState } from 'react'


export const DynamicFlexDirection = () => {
    const [direction, setDirection] = useState('row')
    return (
        <Flex direction='column' gap='lg'>
            <Flex gap='sm'>
                <Text as='span'>Change Direction Value:</Text>
                <Button size='sm' variant={direction === 'row' ? 'flat' : null} onPress={() => {setDirection('row')}}>row</Button>
                <Button size='sm' variant={direction === 'row-reverse' ? 'flat' : null} onPress={() => {setDirection('row-reverse')}}>row-reverse</Button>
                <Button size='sm' variant={direction === 'column' ? 'flat' : null} onPress={() => {setDirection('column')}}>column</Button>
                <Button size='sm' variant={direction === 'column-reverse' ? 'flat' : null} onPress={() => {setDirection('column-reverse')}}>column-reverse</Button>
            </Flex>
            <Flex direction={direction} gap='md'>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>01</div>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>02</div>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>03</div>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>04</div>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>05</div>
            </Flex>
        </Flex>
    )
}

import Text from '@zyxui/text'
import Button from '@zyxui/button'
import { useState } from 'react'


export const DynamicFlexDirection = () => {
    const [direction, setDirection] = useState('row')
    return (
        <Flex direction='column' gap='lg'>
            <Flex gap='sm'>
                <Text as='span'>Change Direction Value:</Text>
                <Button size='sm' variant={direction === 'row' ? 'flat' : null} onPress={() => {setDirection('row')}}>row</Button>
                <Button size='sm' variant={direction === 'row-reverse' ? 'flat' : null} onPress={() => {setDirection('row-reverse')}}>row-reverse</Button>
                <Button size='sm' variant={direction === 'column' ? 'flat' : null} onPress={() => {setDirection('column')}}>column</Button>
                <Button size='sm' variant={direction === 'column-reverse' ? 'flat' : null} onPress={() => {setDirection('column-reverse')}}>column-reverse</Button>
            </Flex>
            <Flex direction={direction} gap='md'>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>01</div>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>02</div>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>03</div>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>04</div>
                <div className='bg-pink-800 px-10 py-2'>05</div>
            </Flex>
        </Flex>
    )
}

import Text from '@zyxui/text';
import Flex from '@zyxui/flex';
import { useState } from 'react';

const DynamicFlexGap = () => {
    const [gap, setGap] = useState('md')

    return (
        <>
            <Flex direction='column' className='mb-5'>
                <Text as={'p'}>Gap Sizes:</Text>
                <Flex gap='md'>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={!gap ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap(undefined)}>None</Button>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={gap === 'sm' ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap('sm')}>sm</Button>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={gap === 'md' ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap('md')}>md</Button>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={gap === 'lg' ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap('lg')}>lg</Button>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={gap === 'xl' ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap('xl')}>xl</Button>
                </Flex>
            </Flex>
            <Flex gap={gap}>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
            </Flex>
        </>
    )
}

export default DynamicFlexGap;

Button from '@zyxui/button';
import Text from '@zyxui/text';
import Flex from '@zyxui/flex';
import { useState } from 'react';

const DynamicFlexGap = () => {
    const [gap, setGap] = useState('md')

    return (
        <>
            <Flex direction='column' className='mb-5'>
                <Text as={'p'}>Gap Sizes:</Text>
                <Flex gap='md'>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={!gap ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap(undefined)}>None</Button>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={gap === 'sm' ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap('sm')}>sm</Button>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={gap === 'md' ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap('md')}>md</Button>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={gap === 'lg' ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap('lg')}>lg</Button>
                    <Button size={'sm'} variant={gap === 'xl' ? 'solid' : 'flat'} onPress={() => setGap('xl')}>xl</Button>
                </Flex>
            </Flex>
            <Flex gap={gap}>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
                <Button>Button</Button>
            </Flex>
        </>
    )
}

export default DynamicFlexGap;

# Input The `Input` component is a comprehensive form control that provides users with a text input field. It includes support for various states, validation, accessibility features, and customization options. Built with React Aria for maximum accessibility compliance. ## Installation Ensure that you have the @zyxui library installed in your project: ```bash npm install @zyxui/input ``` If you haven't installed and setup @zyxui before, please follow the [`installation guide`](/docs/installation) ## Basic Input To create a basic input, simply use the Input component with a placeholder. It will inherit the default styling. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; export const BasicInputExample = () => { return ( ) } ``` ## Customization The `Input` component is **highly customizable**, allowing you to fine-tune its appearance and behavior to align with your project's unique requirements. Explore the following customization options: ### With Label Add a label to your input for better accessibility and user experience. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; export const LabeledInputExample = () => { return ( <> ) } ``` ### Variants Modify `Input` styles effortlessly using the `variant` prop, with options like `default`, `filled`, `underlined`, and `bordered`. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; export const InputVariantsExample = () => { return ( <> ) } ``` ### Sizes Resize your `inputs` effortlessly with the size prop. Choose from `sm` (Small), `md` (Medium), or `lg` (Large) to control the input dimensions. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; export const InputSizesExample = () => { return ( <> ) } ``` ### States Display different states for validation feedback using the `state` prop and `errorMessage`. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; export const InputStatesExample = () => { return ( <> ) } ``` ### Start Content The `startContent` prop allows you to add icons or other elements at the beginning of the input field. } label="Username" placeholder="Enter username" /> } label="Email" placeholder="Enter email" type="email" /> } label="Search" placeholder="Search..." /> ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; import { UserIcon, MailIcon, SearchIcon } from 'lucide-react'; export const InputStartContentExample = () => { return ( <> } label="Username" placeholder="Enter username" /> } label="Email" placeholder="Enter email" type="email" /> } label="Search" placeholder="Search..." /> ) } ``` ### End Content The `endContent` prop allows you to add elements at the end of the input field, such as action buttons or status indicators. } label="Password" type="password" placeholder="Enter password" /> @domain.com} label="Email" placeholder="username" /> ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; import { EyeIcon } from 'lucide-react'; export const InputEndContentExample = () => { return ( <> } label="Password" type="password" placeholder="Enter password" /> @domain.com} label="Email" placeholder="username" /> ) } ``` ### Clearable Enable the clearable functionality to allow users to quickly clear the input value. } label="Search" placeholder="Search..." /> ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; import { SearchIcon } from 'lucide-react'; export const ClearableInputExample = () => { return ( <> } label="Search" placeholder="Search..." /> ) } ``` ### Required Fields Mark fields as required for better form validation and user guidance. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; export const RequiredInputExample = () => { return ( <> ) } ``` ### Disabled State Show disabled inputs for read-only or inactive form fields. ```jsx showLineNumbers import Input from '@zyxui/input'; export const DisabledInputExample = () => { return ( <> ) } ``` ## Advanced Usage ### Form Integration The Input component works seamlessly with form libraries and includes built-in validation support.

| Placeholder text | | `variant` | `'default' \| 'filled' \| 'underlined' \| 'bordered'` | `'default'` | Input style variant | | `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Input size | | `state` | `'default' \| 'error' \| 'success' \| 'warning'` | `'default'` | Input state for validation | | `radius` | `'none' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'full'` | `'md'` | Border radius | | `startContent` | `ReactNode` | - | Content to display at the start of the input | | `endContent` | `ReactNode` | - | Content to display at the end of the input | | `helperText` | `string` | - | Helper text below the input | | `errorMessage` | `string` | - | Error message (overrides helperText) | | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the field is required | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the input is disabled | | `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to show a clear button | | `onClear` | `() => void` | - | Callback when clear button is clicked | | `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the input | | `containerClassName` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the container | | `labelClassName` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the label | The Input component also accepts all standard HTML input attributes through React Aria's `AriaTextFieldOptions`. ## Accessibility The Input component is built with accessibility in mind: - ✅ **Keyboard Navigation**: Full keyboard support for all interactions - ✅ **Screen Reader Support**: Proper ARIA labels and descriptions - ✅ **Focus Management**: Clear focus indicators and logical tab order - ✅ **Error Handling**: Accessible error messages and validation states - ✅ **Required Fields**: Clear indication of required fields ## Best Practices 1. **Always provide labels** for better accessibility 2. **Use appropriate input types** (email, password, etc.) 3. **Provide helpful error messages** that guide users to fix issues 4. **Use helper text** to clarify input expectations 5. **Group related inputs** logically in forms 6. **Test with keyboard navigation** and screen readers

      <Input
        required
        label="Full Name"
        placeholder="Enter your full name"
        startContent={<UserIcon size={16} />}

        required
        type="email"
        label="Email Address"
        placeholder="Enter your email"

      <Input
        required
        type="password"
        label="Password"
        placeholder="Create a password"
        startContent={<LockIcon size={16} />}
        helperText="Must be at least 8 characters"
      />
    </form>
  )
}

        label="Full Name"
        placeholder="Enter your full name"

      />
    </form>
  )
}

import Text from '@zyxui/text' # Text Component `Text` component will be useful to display texts on your website. This component will help you to customize your texts easily and fast. ## Installation Ensure that have the @zyxui library installed in your project: ```bash npm install @zyxui/text ``` If you haven't install and setup @zyxui before please follow the [`installation guide`](/docs/installation) ## Basic Text You can use text without passing any props.

code ) } ``` ## Customization ### as `as` prop can make you able to switch between element type. There are many element types that have been added to `Text` component: ### Headings You can switch between Heading by passing `as` prop. Available heading props are `h1` | `h2` | `h3` | `h4` | `h5` , and `h6`

import { Preview, Example, Command } from '@/components/mdx/components'; import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from '@zyxui/tabs'; import Button from '@zyxui/button'; import Card from '@zyxui/card'; import Avatar from '@zyxui/avatar'; import Badge from '@zyxui/badge'; import Text from '@zyxui/text'; import { User, Settings, CreditCard, Bell } from 'lucide-react'; # Tabs The `Tabs` component provides a way to organize content into multiple sections that can be accessed through tab triggers. It supports multiple variants, orientations, and is fully accessible with keyboard navigation and ARIA attributes. ## Installation Ensure that you have the @zyxui library installed in your project: ```bash pnpm add @zyxui/tabs ``` If you haven't installed and setup @zyxui before, please follow the [`installation guide`](/docs/installation) ## Basic Tabs The most basic usage of the Tabs component consists of a Tabs container, TabsList for the tab triggers, TabsTrigger for individual tabs, and TabsContent for the content panels. ```jsx showLineNumbers import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from '@zyxui/tabs'; import { User, Settings, CreditCard, Bell } from 'lucide-react'; import Card from '@zyxui/card'; import Avatar from '@zyxui/avatar'; import Badge from '@zyxui/badge'; import Button from '@zyxui/button'; import Text from '@zyxui/text'; export const UserDashboardExample = () => { return ( Overview Billing Notifications Settings {/* Dashboard content */} {/* Billing content */} {/* Notifications content */} {/* Settings content */} ) } ``` ## Controlled Usage For advanced use cases where you need to control the tab state programmatically, you can use the `value` and `onValueChange` props instead of `defaultValue`. ```jsx showLineNumbers import { useState } from 'react'; import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from '@zyxui/tabs'; export const ControlledTabsExample = () => { const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState('step1'); return (
Step 1 Step 2 Step 3

Step 1: Information

Current tab: {activeTab}

Step 2: Confirmation

Current tab: {activeTab}

Step 3: Complete

Current tab: {activeTab}

) } ``` ## API Reference ### Tabs The root tabs component that provides context to all child components. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `value` | `string` | - | The controlled value of the tabs | | `defaultValue` | `string` | - | The default value for uncontrolled usage | | `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Callback fired when the tab changes | | `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | The orientation of the tabs | | `variant` | `'default' \| 'underline' \| 'pills'` | `'default'` | The visual variant of the tabs | | `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | The size of the tab triggers | | `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes | ### TabsList The container for tab triggers. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes | ### TabsTrigger Individual tab trigger button. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `value` | `string` | - | **Required.** The value that identifies this tab | | `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the tab is disabled | ### TabsContent The content panel for each tab. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `value` | `string` | - | **Required.** The value that identifies this content | | `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes | ## Accessibility The Tabs component follows WAI-ARIA guidelines for accessibility: - **Keyboard Navigation**: Arrow keys navigate between tabs, Home/End keys jump to first/last tab - **Focus Management**: Proper focus indicators and management - **ARIA Attributes**: Uses `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, and `role="tabpanel"` - **Screen Reader Support**: Proper labeling and association between tabs and content - **State Communication**: Active/inactive states are communicated to assistive technologies ### Keyboard Shortcuts - `Arrow Keys`: Navigate between tabs - `Home`: Move to first tab - `End`: Move to last tab - `Space/Enter`: Activate focused tab ## Best Practices 1. **Use descriptive tab labels** that clearly indicate the content 2. **Limit the number of tabs** to avoid overwhelming users (5-7 tabs maximum recommended) 3. **Consider vertical orientation** for side navigation patterns 4. **Provide loading states** for content that needs to be fetched 5. **Use controlled tabs** when you need to programmatically change the active tab 6. **Ensure content is accessible** in all tab panels

        </TabsContent>

        <TabsList>
          <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>

          <TabsTrigger value="settings">Settings</TabsTrigger>

          <p className="text-center py-6">Overview content with underline styling</p>
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="details">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Details content</p>
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="settings">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Settings content</p>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>

      {/* Pills Variant */}
      <Tabs defaultValue="overview" variant="pills">
        <TabsList>
          <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="details">Details</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="settings">Settings</TabsTrigger>

        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="settings">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Settings content</p>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>
    </>
  )
}

          <p className="text-center py-6">Another tab</p>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>

      <Tabs defaultValue="tab1" size="lg">
        <TabsList>
          <TabsTrigger value="tab1">Large</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="tab2">Tabs</TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>
        <TabsContent value="tab1">
          <p className="text-center py-8">Large size content</p>
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="tab2">
          <p className="text-center py-8">Another tab</p>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>
    </>
  )
}

{ Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from '@zyxui/tabs';

export const TabsOrientationExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      {/* Horizontal */}
      <Tabs defaultValue="profile" orientation="horizontal">
        <TabsList>
          <TabsTrigger value="profile">Profile</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="account">Account</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="settings">Settings</TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>
        <TabsContent value="profile">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Profile settings content</p>
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="account">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Account management content</p>
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="settings">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Application settings</p>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>

      {/* Vertical */}
      <Tabs defaultValue="profile" orientation="vertical" className="flex">
        <TabsList className="flex-col h-fit">
          <TabsTrigger value="profile">Profile</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="account">Account</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="settings">Settings</TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>
        <TabsContent value="profile">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Profile settings content</p>
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="account">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Account management content</p>
        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="settings">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Application settings</p>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>
    </>
  )
}

        </TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value="settings">
          <p className="text-center py-6">Application settings</p>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>
    </>
  )
}

          <Settings className="w-4 h-4 mr-2" />
          Settings
        </TabsTrigger>

      <TabsContent value="overview" className="space-y-4">
        {/* Dashboard content */}

        {/* Notifications content */}
      </TabsContent>

      <TabsContent value="settings" className="space-y-4">
        {/* Settings content */}
      </TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  )
}

        {/* Notifications content */}
      </TabsContent>

      <TabsContent value="settings" className="space-y-4">
        {/* Settings content */}
      </TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  )
}

`,(0,n.jsxDEV)(e.div,{"data-rehype-pretty-code-fragment":"",children:[(0,n.jsxDEV)(e.pre,{className:"vitesse-light",style:{backgroundColor:"#ffffff"},tabIndex:"0","data-language":"jsx","data-theme":"light",raw:`import { useState } from 'react';
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from '@zyxui/tabs';

export const ControlledTabsExample = () => {
  const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState('step1');

  return (
    <div className="space-y-4">
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <button onClick={() => setActiveTab('step1')}>Go to Step 1</button>
        <button onClick={() => setActiveTab('step2')}>Go to Step 2</button>
        <button onClick={() => setActiveTab('step3')}>Go to Step 3</button>
      </div>

      <Tabs value={activeTab} onValueChange={setActiveTab}>
        <TabsList className="grid w-full grid-cols-3">
          <TabsTrigger value="step1">Step 1</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="step2">Step 2</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="step3">Step 3</TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>

        <TabsContent value="step1">
          <div className="p-6 text-center">
            <h3 className="font-semibold mb-2">Step 1: Information</h3>
            <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
              Current tab: {activeTab}
            </p>
          </div>
        </TabsContent>

        <TabsContent value="step2">
          <div className="p-6 text-center">
            <h3 className="font-semibold mb-2">Step 2: Confirmation</h3>
            <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
              Current tab: {activeTab}
            </p>
          </div>
        </TabsContent>

        <TabsContent value="step3">
          <div className="p-6 text-center">
            <h3 className="font-semibold mb-2">Step 3: Complete</h3>
            <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
              Current tab: {activeTab}
            </p>
          </div>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>
    </div>
  )
}

import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from '@zyxui/tabs';

export const ControlledTabsExample = () => {
  const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState('step1');

  return (
    <div className="space-y-4">
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <button onClick={() => setActiveTab('step1')}>Go to Step 1</button>
        <button onClick={() => setActiveTab('step2')}>Go to Step 2</button>
        <button onClick={() => setActiveTab('step3')}>Go to Step 3</button>
      </div>

      <Tabs value={activeTab} onValueChange={setActiveTab}>
        <TabsList className="grid w-full grid-cols-3">
          <TabsTrigger value="step1">Step 1</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="step2">Step 2</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value="step3">Step 3</TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>

        <TabsContent value="step1">
          <div className="p-6 text-center">
            <h3 className="font-semibold mb-2">Step 1: Information</h3>
            <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
              Current tab: {activeTab}
            </p>
          </div>
        </TabsContent>

        <TabsContent value="step2">
          <div className="p-6 text-center">
            <h3 className="font-semibold mb-2">Step 2: Confirmation</h3>
            <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
              Current tab: {activeTab}
            </p>
          </div>
        </TabsContent>

        <TabsContent value="step3">
          <div className="p-6 text-center">
            <h3 className="font-semibold mb-2">Step 3: Complete</h3>
            <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
              Current tab: {activeTab}
            </p>
          </div>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>
    </div>
  )
}
